start_here: Say to your AI: "Let <their name> into <my pursuit's database>." They say to theirs: "Join <the pursuit> with a password only I keep."
no_lists_because: Who may work in a pursuit is the database's own logins and grants; these workflows keep no list of members.
instructions: 1. Tell the person the database's address, its name and a login name for them.
2. They run workflow:join-a-pursuit-with-a-password-only-i-keep: their computer makes the password, keeps it in their own vault and sends you only the verifier.
3. You run workflow:let-a-person-into-a-pursuit with database, role and password_verifier (and until, if it should stop on a date).

4. When the pursuit's own owner may not make logins (a computer's pursuit database), also give login_maker: the vault name of the computer's login that may. It makes only the login; the pursuit's owner gives it its rights.
5. Every change they make is told with their login as who made it.
6. To end it, run workflow:take-a-person-out-of-a-pursuit with database and role; their changes stay.

worked_examples.title: Let a coach into the club's database
worked_examples.ask: Let Sam into the club database; Sam sent role sam_coach and a verifier.
worked_examples.given: The database has no login sam_coach.
worked_examples.hands_back: role "sam_coach", valid_until "infinity"; then database "club", address "203.0.113.7", port 5432 and said "sam_coach may now work in club. Every change they make is told as theirs; workflow:take-a-person-out-of-a-pursuit ends it."
